answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost.
